Schedule 2-week pilot benchmark and agree eval parity criteria
action_items: Miles Chen: send pricing + sizing worksheet by 2026-03-05
Priya Raman: prepare benchmark config, perf checklist and vLLM/TGI compatibility notes by 2026-03-06

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: 48 minutes (scheduled)
- Attendees: Miles Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Leo Park (CTO), Maria Gomez (Lead ML Eng), Jared Kim (Infra Eng)

Summary: initial migration discovery for Orison Labs evaluating Redwood Dedicated (and Private) as a replacement for OpenAI hosted endpoints. Key concerns: eval parity, latency/cost tradeoffs, vLLM/TGI compatibility, private VPC networking, SOC2/KMS, and pilot benchmarks.

Links referenced: Redwood deck (shared): https://redwood.ai/deck/orison-deck, benchmark sheet: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/orison-bench.xlsx, security package stub: https://redwood.ai/security/orison-package.pdf

Transcript:
[00:00] Miles: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Miles Chen, I'm the AE on the account, joining from Redwood HQ.
[00:08] Priya: hi all, Priya Raman, solutions engineering. I'll be covering the deep tech bits and the perf bits.
[00:14] Leo: hi Miles, Priya. Leo here, CTO at Orison. Maria and Jared are on too. thanks for doing this.
[00:21] Maria: hi, thanks.
[00:23] Jared: hey.
[00:25] Miles: quick agenda — hear about your current infra and pain points, where you're seeing cost/latency issues with OpenAI, compatibility questions (vLLM/TGI), talk through Redwood Dedicated and Private options, and next steps for a pilot. does that sound good?
[00:36] Leo: sounds good. we have a lot to get through.

[00:40] Maria: to start, we're running most prod traffic on OpenAI right now, with a mix of gpt-4 style calls and smaller 3.5-ish embeds. monthly spend is about $200k. we also run an internal TGI/vLLM stack for some latency-sensitive inference, but the results between TGI and OpenAI are not identical — eval parity is our big worry.
[01:02] Priya: when you say not identical, is that at the hallucination / instruction-following level or perf / latency?
[01:08] Maria: both, but mostly quality. a couple of prompts degrade when we move to local models. we also saw tokenization differences causing off-by-one behaviors in our scoring.
[01:17] Miles: mm-hmm. that's super common, yeah. Redwood's approach for Dedicated is to support the same API surface and provide model variants and tuning to match evals. we also surface quantization and kernel choices so you can pick the trade-off you want.
[01:30] Leo: can you clarify what you mean by "same API surface"? our engineers use OpenAI SDKs pretty heavily. we don't want a big rewrite.
[01:37] Priya: good question. Redwood provides a drop-in compatible REST/SDK layer — most customers keep their existing client code and change the endpoint and keys. there are some model name mappings, but we try to keep behavior consistent. small differences around decoding defaults and tokenization may need adjustments; we document those.
[01:56] Maria: ok, good. next, the infra side — our infra team manages noisy-neighbor concerns and latency; how does Dedicated differ from just running vLLM/TGI on our own infra?
[02:07] Priya: two big differences: one, we run a GPU-optimized inference runtime with kernel selection, continuous batching, and KV cache management so that you get better throughput/latency than vanilla vLLM/TGI in many configs; two, we provide orchestration, autoscaling, and the ability to pin models / rollouts and automatic fallback policies. so it's more opinionated.
[02:28] Jared: do you support customers bringing their own vLLM or TGI images?
[02:32] Priya: you can bring models and in many cases bring model containers, but we recommend using Redwood-verified model variants for production; if you bring a custom vLLM runtime, we'll validate compatibility. there is sometimes engineering work to make sure the runtime is using the same tokenizers and kernel paths.
[02:48] Leo: ok, about compliance — we need SOC 2, SSO with our IdP, audit logs, KMS integration — and we might need on-prem for some clients — can Redwood handle that?
[02:58] Miles: yes. Dedicated and Private support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integrations. for on-prem air-gapped deployments we have a Private offering, but it is a heavier lift and has a different licensing model. we'll share the security package after the call.
[03:12] Maria: can you share SLA numbers for Dedicated? availability and p99 latency targets?
[03:17] Miles: Dedicated has SLA packages; typical p99 generation latency targets depend on model and seq length — we'll put concrete examples in the pricing + sizing worksheet. for planning, think ~100-200ms p50 for small chat-ish models and p99s that vary with load; we'll propose targets tailored to your prompt profile.
[03:33] Jared: about cost — is the cost model per-token like OpenAI or different? we want predictable forecasting.
[03:39] Miles: we have usage-based pricing for hosted, and reserved capacity/committed contracts for Dedicated. Dedicated pricing includes a commit for a pool of GPUs and throughput; you'll get a predictable monthly rate plus overage terms. we'll send a sizing worksheet so you can map current OpenAI spend to Dedicated commit scenarios.
[03:56] Maria: perfect. now benchmarks — can you run our eval sets? we need eval parity proof; we have a 1000-prompt test set and a set of scoring rubrics.
[04:04] Priya: absolutely. typical flow is you share your eval prompts and scoring; we run them on candidate models (Redwood-verified and any custom checkpoints you bring) and report output-level diffs. if you need exact parity we can iterate on decoding, temperature, sampling and where needed fine-tune or apply post-processing.
[04:22] Maria: how do you handle deterministic reproducibility? some of our scoring requires stable outputs across runs.
[04:27] Priya: we support fixed seeds and deterministic sampling modes where the runtime and model support it; we'll surface the config in the benchmark. note some models don't support perfectly deterministic sampling depending on kernel/quantization choices.
[04:40] Leo: what about prefix/KV caching — we rely on caching heavily to reduce cost at runtime. does Redwood replicate that behavior?
[04:47] Priya: yes, we have prefix caching and KV cache management — can cache hot contexts and route requests to the right shard. that reduces per-token cost and latency for repeated conversational contexts.
[04:57] Jared: any differences running in Private/VPC vs Dedicated hosted in terms of features?
[05:02] Miles: feature parity is the goal; Private has an ops surface where the customer owns more of the infra and networking. some managed services (like Redwood-managed autoscaling) are replaced with customer-managed tooling in on-prem. we'll call that out explicitly in the security doc.
[05:16] Maria: earlier you said kernel selection and quantization — can you talk specifics? we try int8 quantization on vLLM and saw a big perf win but some quality drop.
[05:25] Priya: sure. Redwood's runtime supports multiple quantization paths — int8 / int4 / mixed — and different kernels for attention. we recommend running evals across quantization modes; often int8 gets you a 2-3x inference throughput improvement with minimal quality regression for certain models, but it depends on prompts. we also do per-model tuning to reduce regressions.
[05:46] Leo: do you have customers who moved off OpenAI entirely? any case studies?
[05:50] Miles: yes, we have a couple of mid-market and enterprise customers who did full migrations — cost dropped significantly and latency improved for their conversational routes. i'll share a short case study after the call.
[05:58] Maria: about bringing our own models — we have some internal fine-tuned checkpoints. is Redwood okay running those?
[06:04] Priya: yes, we can run customer checkpoints; we'll do an onboarding validation step and help with conversion of tokenizers and any ops needed. sometimes we recommend keeping the checkpoint but using a Redwood runtime-optimized variant for perf.
[06:17] Jared: any constraints on sequence length or kv cache sizes? we have long context windows for agent-style prompts.
[06:23] Priya: we support long context windows; the limits depend on rack/hardware choice and model architecture. for very long contexts we recommend specific hardware profiles; we'll include recommended configs in the sizing doc.
[06:35] Leo: latency vs cost — typical trade-offs and levers?
[06:38] Miles: batching and caching reduce unit cost but can hurt tail latency; quantization and model distillation reduce cost and improve throughput with potential quality tradeoffs. routing policies can send low-latency traffic to higher-tier pools. Redwood Optimize suggests per-route profiles so you get the right balance.
[06:53] Maria: on the integration side, what's the rollout path? can we do canary or A/B?
[06:57] Priya: yes, our Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies if a model degrades. we wire that into tracing and cost dashboards so you can correlate regressions with a specific model rollout.
[07:10] Leo: cool. any particular gotchas with tokenization differences vs OpenAI?
[07:14] Priya: tokenization sometimes causes off-by-one counts or different truncation behavior. we run tokenization diff tests and have mapping layers for common OpenAI model names. in bench runs we'll highlight token counts so you can adjust scoring.
[07:27] Maria: what about driver-level compatibility: we use the OpenAI SDK across services and have middleware handling retries and rate limits — is there anything special?
[07:36] Miles: not really, most middleware keeps working. we also support per-route quotas and rate limiting so early/backoff logic behaves similarly.
[07:44] Jared: curious about fallback policies — e.g., if Dedicated pool is saturated can it fall back to Redwood hosted or a smaller model?
[07:50] Priya: yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or to hosted as a safety net. policies are configurable by latency, cost, or region.
[08:01] Maria: hmm — security again: do you have an SOC 2 cert? how old is it?
[08:05] Miles: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we keep our reports current; we'll attach the report in the security package. we also have ISO stuff in progress; we'll include what we can.
[08:16] Leo: for the pilot, what do you suggest as a scope? we want to know cost parity and eval parity within two weeks.
[08:22] Priya: typical pilot is 2 weeks: we run your 1k eval prompts across candidate models and a small live traffic sample on a dedicated pool configured to match your workload. deliverables: perf numbers, cost estimates, output diffs, and a recommended Dedicated commit size.
[08:38] Miles: timeline-wise, if you can share evals and traffic samples by Friday (2026-03-06), we can aim for kickoff next week and deliver results by ~2026-03-20.
[08:48] Maria: that would work. a question — do you support partial migrations? for example embeddings on hosted but chat on Dedicated?
[08:55] Miles: yes, hybrid is common: embeddings or low-risk routes stay on hosted while latency-sensitive generation moves to Dedicated. routing policies let you split traffic by route.
[09:07] Jared: operationally, what visibility do we get into token-level cost? we need to show finance a breakdown by product team.
[09:13] Priya: Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards and you can export data. it maps to project or team tags so finance can billback.
[09:25] Leo: all right, last few: SSO — we use Okta; is setup straightforward?
[09:30] Miles: yes, Okta SAML flows are supported. we'll include an SSO kickoff checklist.
[09:36] Maria: and what about data residency? some customers require EU-only.
[09:40] Miles: we have region controls and private options — for strict residency we recommend Private or a Dedicated cluster in the target region.
[09:49] Maria: thanks. returning to perf: do you have sample p99 numbers for the model family we use? we mainly use GPT-4-ish equivalent.
[09:57] Priya: i'll put model-level p50 and p99 examples in the sizing worksheet but to ballpark for a 2k-seq context on a high-throughput pool you might see p99 in the 700-1200ms range depending on model and quantization; if you route to a high-priority pool and adjust batching you can push p99 down.
[10:18] Leo: ok that's helpful. any concerns about vendor lock if we adopt Dedicated? we want the ability to move between providers later.
[10:26] Miles: we prioritize portability — we support standard checkpoints and model exports. Dedicated is primarily an ops/commit contract but you can move models and use the same eval harnesses to compare alternatives.
[10:36] Maria: one nit: when you say "Redwood-verified models" are those open models or proprietary?
[10:41] Priya: mostly curated open checkpoints with performance profiles; Redwood may also provide tuned variants for customers under license. we'll call out provenance in the model catalog.
[10:51] Jared: what about monitoring — do we get token-level tracing?
[10:55] Priya: yes, tracing hooks and per-request metadata are available; you can push traces to your observability backend.
[11:03] Leo: great. anything else on your side?
[11:06] Maria: i think that's the key stuff. i have one more question — how do you handle model rollbacks if eval drift occurs post-rollout?
[11:14] Priya: we have automated rollback policies tied to eval regression alerts and canary thresholds; if a rollout triggers regressions we'll auto-switch to the previous model and create an alert in Console.
[11:24] Miles: ok, to recap next steps: we'll send the pricing/sizing worksheet and security package; Priya will prepare the benchmark config; Orison will share evals and traffic samples by Friday; we'll schedule the pilot kickoff for around 2026-03-10.
[11:36] Leo: sounds good. thanks, Miles, Priya.
[11:39] Maria: thanks.
[11:40] Miles: thanks everyone — we'll follow up by EOD with the materials.

Notes on transcription quality: some words may be mis-transcribed (vLLM sometimes appears as v-L-L-M in notes, TGI as T-G-I). occasional speaker labels simplified.

End of transcript.
